text: A square matrix Y defines the linear map eⱼ↦Σᵢeᵢ⊗Yᵢⱼ on the finite column module, following the convention of [Milne, Remark 4.1](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=95). At this stage Y is arbitrary and its entries need only form an R-module. The name denotes a candidate coaction map; coassociativity and the counit law require the later matrix identities. Checks pass: [matrixCoact_apply_basisFun](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MatrixCoefficient/FromMatrix.lean#L55), [standardCoact_apply_basisFun](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/StandardComodule.lean#L74).
The constructed linear map has the prescribed column value.
The generic GL matrix gives the actual standard coaction columns.

The candidate matrix coaction sends the jth standard basis vector to the tensor sum of column j. This is the column convention in [Milne, Remark 4.1](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=95), proved by the universal property of the standard basis. The finite index type makes the sum finite; the formula alone does not assert that an arbitrary matrix satisfies the comodule axioms. Checks pass: [matrixComodule_coact](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MatrixCoefficient/FromMatrix.lean#L193), [coefficientMatrix_matrixComodule](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MatrixCoefficient/FromMatrix.lean#L202).
When the matrix identities hold, the packaged comodule retains this candidate map.
The reconstructed comodule recovers the original matrix, confirming the index convention.

The matrix coproduct identity is equivalent to Δ(Yᵢⱼ)=ΣₖYᵢₖ⊗Yₖⱼ entrywise, as in [Milne, Remark 4.1](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=95). The index set is finite. Matrix multiplication occurs in the tensor-product algebra: (a⊗1)(1⊗b)=a⊗b. The proof therefore preserves coefficient order and does not require the bialgebra itself to be commutative. Checks pass: [map_comul_map](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MatrixCoefficient/FromMatrix.lean#L108), [comul_coefficientMatrix_eq_sum](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MatrixCoefficient/Matrix.lean#L115).
A bialgebra map preserves the matrix coproduct condition.
Actual comodule coefficients satisfy exactly the ordered entrywise formula.

Applying the counit entrywise gives the identity matrix exactly when ε(Yᵢⱼ)=δᵢⱼ for every pair of indices, matching [Milne, Remark 4.1](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=95). This is an entrywise equality, so no finite index type is needed. Decidable equality supplies the displayed choice between 1 and 0; no determinant or matrix multiplication is involved. Checks pass: [map_counit_map](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MatrixCoefficient/FromMatrix.lean#L134), [counit_coefficientMatrix](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MatrixCoefficient/Matrix.lean#L99).
A bialgebra map preserves the counit matrix equation.
Coefficient matrices of actual comodules have these counit entries.

The counit matrix identity implies ε(Yᵢⱼ)=eⁱ(eⱼ), converting the Kronecker delta into standard-basis coordinates. This is the counit condition needed for reconstruction in [Milne, Remark 4.1](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=95). The finite index hypothesis supplies the standard basis; rewriting its coordinates removes any need for decidable equality from the resulting constructor’s interface. Checks pass: [map_counit_iff](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MatrixCoefficient/FromMatrix.lean#L89), [coefficientMatrix_matrixComodule](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MatrixCoefficient/FromMatrix.lean#L202).
The matrix equation is equivalent to the Kronecker-delta entry formula.
The constructor using those basis-coordinate values recovers the input matrix.

A finite matrix satisfying the coproduct and counit equations defines a right comodule on the column module, with eⱼ↦Σᵢeᵢ⊗Yᵢⱼ. This is the reconstruction direction of [Milne, Remark 4.1](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=95). The two supplied identities prove the two comodule laws; the bialgebra assumptions do not include an antipode or invertibility of Y. Checks pass: [matrixComodule_coact](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MatrixCoefficient/FromMatrix.lean#L193), [coefficientMatrix_matrixComodule](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MatrixCoefficient/FromMatrix.lean#L202).
The packaged structure uses exactly the candidate column coaction.
Taking coefficients of that structure returns Y.

The coaction of the explicitly constructed matrix comodule is the candidate column map matrixCoact. This ties the packaged structure to the formula in [Milne, Remark 4.1](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=95); the supplied matrix identities justify its laws without modifying the map. The equation concerns this chosen comodule structure, since the same column module can carry other coactions. Checks pass: [matrixCoact_apply_basisFun](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MatrixCoefficient/FromMatrix.lean#L55), [coefficientMatrix_matrixComodule](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MatrixCoefficient/FromMatrix.lean#L202).
The identified map has the prescribed columns.
Its standard-basis coefficient matrix is the supplied matrix.

Reconstructing a comodule from Y and then extracting coefficients in the standard basis returns Y itself. Coordinate functionals select the entries of each column, giving the inverse construction in [Milne, Remark 4.1](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=95). The coproduct and counit hypotheses remain necessary to construct the comodule; the theorem does not assign arbitrary matrices a valid coaction. Checks pass: [matrixCoact_apply_basisFun](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MatrixCoefficient/FromMatrix.lean#L55), [coefficientMatrix_basisFun](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/StandardComodule.lean#L102).
The candidate coaction inserts precisely the columns of Y.
The actual standard GL comodule recovers its generic matrix.

This is the set of individual coefficients c(φ,m), obtained by varying a linear functional and a vector. It supplies the generators of the coefficient space described in [Milne, coefficient coalgebra, p.237](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=248). A member must have one such pair as a witness; closure under sums or multiplication is added separately by the span and generated-algebra constructions. Checks pass: [mem_matrixCoefficientSet_iff](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MatrixCoefficient/Adjoin.lean#L79), [groupLike_mem_rankOne_matrixCoefficientSet](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MatrixCoefficient/Trivial.lean#L78).
Membership has exactly a functional/vector witness.
The coefficient of the identity functional at 1 realizes the group-like generator.

Every coefficient c(φ,m) belongs to the coefficient set, with the pair (φ,m) as its witness. This records the generators used for the coefficient space in [Milne, coefficient coalgebra, p.237](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=248). The statement concerns individual coefficients before taking linear combinations, so it requires neither a finite basis nor any multiplication on the ambient coalgebra. Checks pass: [mem_matrixCoefficientSet_iff](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MatrixCoefficient/Adjoin.lean#L79), [groupLike_mem_rankOne_matrixCoefficientSet](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MatrixCoefficient/Trivial.lean#L78).
The membership characterization exposes the same witness pair.
The rank-one homogeneous comodule supplies an explicit generator example.

Membership means precisely that c equals c(φ,m) for some functional φ and vector m. Uncurrying in the definition simply treats this pair as one argument. This identifies the raw generators of [Milne, coefficient coalgebra, p.237](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=248); it does not replace a single coefficient witness by an arbitrary finite linear combination. Checks pass: [matrixCoefficient_mem_set](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MatrixCoefficient/Adjoin.lean#L72), [matrixCoefficientSet_subset_of_surjective](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MatrixCoefficient/Adjoin.lean#L153).
Every witnessed coefficient belongs to the set.
Surjective comodule maps transport these witnesses by lifting the vector and pulling back the functional.

The coefficient submodule is the R-linear span of all c(φ,m), the coefficient space underlying [Milne, coefficient coalgebra, p.237](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=248). Taking a span allows finite sums and scalar multiples even when they are not presented by a single pair. This definition applies to any comodule; finite generation and coproduct stability under stronger hypotheses are separate results. Checks pass: [range_matrixCoefficientTensor](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MatrixCoefficient/Adjoin.lean#L124), [groupLike_rankOne_matrixCoefficientSubmodule_eq_span_singleton](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MatrixCoefficient/Trivial.lean#L86).
The span equals the image of the bilinear coefficient map on M*⊗M.
A rank-one homogeneous comodule has exactly the line spanned by its group-like coefficient.

Each coefficient lies in the linear span used to define the coefficient submodule. This is the generator inclusion for the coefficient space in [Milne, coefficient coalgebra, p.237](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=248); no additional closure argument is required for a single coefficient. The ambient structure needed is a coalgebra over a commutative semiring, without multiplication or a chosen basis. Checks pass: [matrixCoefficientSubmodule_le_iff](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MatrixCoefficient/Adjoin.lean#L116), [groupLike_rankOne_matrixCoefficientSubmodule_eq_span_singleton](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MatrixCoefficient/Trivial.lean#L86).
Containment of every generator characterizes containment of the whole span.
The rank-one example identifies the span concretely.

If a submodule P contains every c(φ,m), it contains their entire linear span. This is the minimality property of the coefficient space in [Milne, coefficient coalgebra, p.237](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=248). The quantified hypothesis ranges over all functionals and vectors; checking only selected basis coefficients would require an additional finite-basis argument that this statement does not assume. Checks pass: [matrixCoefficientSubmodule_le_iff](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MatrixCoefficient/Adjoin.lean#L116), [groupLike_matrixCoefficientSubmodule_le_span_singleton](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MatrixCoefficient/Trivial.lean#L68).
The converse follows from inclusion of each generator.
The universal property proves the concrete containment for a homogeneous coaction.

The image of M*⊗M→C is exactly the span of the individual coefficients, matching [Milne, coefficient coalgebra, p.237](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=248). Elementary tensors generate the tensor product and map to c(φ,m), so their linear combinations give both inclusions. This is an image equality, not injectivity of the coefficient map or an assertion that every tensor is elementary. Checks pass: [matrixCoefficientTensor_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MatrixCoefficient/Basic.lean#L135), [matrixCoefficientSubmodule_le_iff](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MatrixCoefficient/Adjoin.lean#L116).
Each elementary tensor maps to its corresponding coefficient.
The span is characterized by containing all those elementary images.

This is the smallest R-subalgebra containing the coefficients, adding scalar constants, sums and products to their linear span. It is the coefficient-generated algebra operation used in [Milne, Proposition 8.34 proof](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=167). It does not automatically adjoin antipode images or inverses, so it is not asserted to be a Hopf subalgebra or the entire coordinate algebra. Checks pass: [groupLike_rankOne_matrixCoefficientSubalgebra_eq_adjoin_singleton](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MatrixCoefficient/Trivial.lean#L131), [trivial_matrixCoefficientSubalgebra_eq_bot](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MatrixCoefficient/Trivial.lean#L201).
The rank-one homogeneous case gives precisely the algebra generated by its group-like element.
The trivial coaction gives the bottom subalgebra, namely the scalar image.

The defining equation identifies the coefficient algebra with Algebra.adjoin of the raw coefficient set. Here adjoin means unital R-algebra generation, the operation appearing in [Milne, Proposition 8.34 proof](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=167); scalar constants are included even for an empty generating set. It does not mean localization or closure under the Hopf antipode. Checks pass: [matrixCoefficientSubalgebra_le_iff](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MatrixCoefficient/Adjoin.lean#L231), [trivial_matrixCoefficientSubalgebra_eq_bot](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MatrixCoefficient/Trivial.lean#L201).
Its universal property is containment exactly when all coefficients are contained.
The trivial example confirms the scalar-image bottom subalgebra convention.

Every coefficient belongs to the algebra generated by all coefficients. This is the generator inclusion for the algebra construction in [Milne, Proposition 8.34 proof](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=167), requiring an ambient algebra and coalgebra but no compatibility between them. The conclusion is membership only; it supplies neither an inverse of the coefficient nor membership of its antipode image. Checks pass: [matrixCoefficientSubalgebra_le_iff](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MatrixCoefficient/Adjoin.lean#L231), [groupLike_rankOne_matrixCoefficientSubalgebra_eq_adjoin_singleton](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MatrixCoefficient/Trivial.lean#L131).
Containment of the generators characterizes containment of their generated algebra.
The rank-one group-like example identifies the generated algebra explicitly.

An R-subalgebra containing every coefficient contains the coefficient-generated algebra. This is algebraic generation’s minimality property used in [Milne, Proposition 8.34 proof](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=167). Unlike the linear-span version, the target already contains scalar constants and is closed under multiplication; neither antipode stability nor surjectivity onto the ambient algebra is part of the conclusion. Checks pass: [matrixCoefficientSubalgebra_le_iff](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MatrixCoefficient/Adjoin.lean#L231), [groupLike_matrixCoefficientSubalgebra_le_adjoin_singleton](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MatrixCoefficient/Trivial.lean#L121).
The reverse implication is the inclusion of each coefficient generator.
The universal property gives the expected homogeneous-coaction example.

For a finitely generated projective comodule M, its coefficient span is finitely generated: M* is finitely generated, hence so is M*⊗M and its image. This extends the finite-dimensional coefficient-space statement in [Milne, coefficient coalgebra, p.237](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=248). Module.Finite means finite generation, not finite cardinality; projectivity is retained to justify finiteness of the dual. Checks pass: [range_matrixCoefficientTensor](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MatrixCoefficient/Adjoin.lean#L124), [matrixCoefficientSubcoalgebra_finite](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MatrixCoefficient/Subcoalgebra.lean#L91).
The coefficient span is the image of the tensor coefficient map.
The finite-free specialization gives the same finite underlying coefficient module.

For finite free M, the coefficient span D satisfies Δ(D)⊆im(D⊗D→C⊗C), by the ordered coefficient coproduct formula. This matches [Milne, coefficient coalgebra, p.237](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=248) over fields. The formal subcoalgebra stores this tensor-image stability; over general semirings it does not assert injectivity of the tensor inclusion or install a coalgebra structure on D. Checks pass: [comul_matrixCoefficient_eq_sum](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MatrixCoefficient/Comul.lean#L135), [matrixCoefficientSubcoalgebra_toSubmodule](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MatrixCoefficient/Subcoalgebra.lean#L83).
Each coefficient coproduct is a sum of tensors of coefficients.
The underlying carrier is exactly the original coefficient span.

The coefficient subcoalgebra has exactly the coefficient span as its underlying submodule, with no enlargement during packaging. This identifies the carrier described in [Milne, coefficient coalgebra, p.237](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=248). The construction adds a proof that coproducts lie in the tensor-inclusion image; the finite basis chosen to prove that property does not alter the carrier. Checks pass: [mem_matrixCoefficientSubcoalgebra](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MatrixCoefficient/Subcoalgebra.lean#L98), [matrixCoefficientSubcoalgebra_le_iff](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MatrixCoefficient/Subcoalgebra.lean#L131).
Element membership is exactly membership in the same span.
The packaged subobject retains the expected minimality among subcoalgebras.

The underlying module of the coefficient subcoalgebra is finitely generated because it is the coefficient span of a finite free comodule. This is the finite-dimensional conclusion of [Milne, coefficient coalgebra, p.237](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=248) generalized to semirings. The result says Module.Finite, not that the carrier has finitely many elements or that this submodule is itself free. Checks pass: [matrixCoefficientSubcoalgebra_toSubmodule](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MatrixCoefficient/Subcoalgebra.lean#L83), [matrixCoefficientSubmodule_finite](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MatrixCoefficient/Finite.lean#L42).
The subcoalgebra carrier is the coefficient span.
The stronger finite-projective theorem proves finite generation of that span.

An element belongs to the coefficient subcoalgebra exactly when it belongs to the coefficient span. This expresses the carrier identification in [Milne, coefficient coalgebra, p.237](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=248), since the construction adds coproduct-stability evidence without changing elements. Membership allows finite linear combinations of coefficients; it does not demand a single functional/vector pair representing the element. Checks pass: [matrixCoefficientSubcoalgebra_toSubmodule](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MatrixCoefficient/Subcoalgebra.lean#L83), [matrixCoefficient_mem_subcoalgebra](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MatrixCoefficient/Subcoalgebra.lean#L106).
The underlying submodule is exactly the coefficient span.
Every individual coefficient satisfies this membership condition.

Every coefficient c(φ,m) lies in the coefficient subcoalgebra of a finite free comodule, because it lies in the defining span. This is the generator inclusion for [Milne, coefficient coalgebra, p.237](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=248). The finite-free hypotheses construct the subcoalgebra’s coproduct-stability proof; membership itself uses the span inclusion and does not claim the coefficient is group-like. Checks pass: [mem_matrixCoefficientSubcoalgebra](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MatrixCoefficient/Subcoalgebra.lean#L98), [matrixCoefficientSubcoalgebra_le_iff](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MatrixCoefficient/Subcoalgebra.lean#L131).
Membership reduces to membership in the coefficient span.
Containment of all these generators characterizes containment of the subcoalgebra.

A nonnegative real embeds as the same finite value in [0,∞]. The embedding is injective, preserves order, addition and multiplication, and never produces infinity. Its domain already excludes negative numbers; this differs from the real-to-extended-real conversion, which first replaces negative inputs by zero. Compared with [Faris §2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Basic.lean#L117).

A real number is converted to [0,∞] by replacing it with max(r,0) and then embedding that finite nonnegative value. Thus negative inputs become zero and infinity is never produced. This is a clipped conversion, not an injective embedding of all real numbers. Compared with [Faris §§2.6, 8.1](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Basic.lean#L233).

Finite extended nonnegative reals convert to their usual real values, but infinity converts to zero. This total definition is useful only with its finiteness conditions remembered: conversion preserves addition for finite operands, and is not globally order preserving, since 1≤∞ but their converted values are 1 and 0. Compared with [Faris §2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Basic.lean#L230).

Finite extended nonnegative reals convert back to the same nonnegative real, while infinity converts to zero. Consequently, embedding the result recovers the input exactly when the input is finite. The zero result is ambiguous: it can represent either an original zero or an original infinity. Compared with [Faris §2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Basic.lean#L227).

The comparison on [0,∞] agrees with ordinary comparison between finite nonnegative reals and places infinity above every finite value. In particular, infinity≤infinity holds, whereas infinity≤r is false for finite r. This declaration supplies that relation; the subsequent order structures establish its laws. Compared with [Faris §2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Basic.lean#L128).

The extended comparison is reflexive, transitive and antisymmetric, extending the ordinary order on nonnegative reals with a greatest value infinity. These are the partial-order laws supplied here; total comparability also holds for this particular number system, but is packaged separately in its linear-order structure. Compared with [Faris §2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Basic.lean#L128).

Every set of extended nonnegative reals has a supremum and an infimum, and any two values are comparable. Sets of finite values with no finite upper bound have supremum infinity. The empty-set conventions are supremum zero and infimum infinity, as required by the least and greatest elements of [0,∞]. Compared with [Faris §§5.3–5.4](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Basic.lean#L155).

The distinguished top value is positive infinity, an additional point beyond every finite nonnegative real. It is neither an unspecified large real nor the finite zero used by some conversion defaults. This declaration supplies the point; the inherited order makes it the greatest element. Compared with [Faris §2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Basic.lean#L128).

Zero in [0,∞] is the embedded ordinary nonnegative real zero, distinct from infinity. It is the least element and the additive identity under the surrounding structures. Its multiplicative behavior includes 0·∞=0, the analysis convention explicitly used here rather than an indeterminate product. Compared with [Faris §2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Basic.lean#L122).

One in [0,∞] is the embedded ordinary nonnegative real one, so it is finite and distinct from infinity. With the surrounding multiplication it is the multiplicative identity, including 1·∞=∞. The declaration chooses this familiar value; it does not introduce a separate infinite or approximate unit. Compared with [Faris §2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Basic.lean#L123).

Addition on [0,∞] uses ordinary addition for finite nonnegative values and returns infinity whenever either summand is infinity. Hence infinity plus infinity is infinity. There is no negative infinity in this domain, so the ambiguous mixed-infinity sum of the signed extended reals never arises. Compared with [Faris §2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Basic.lean#L128).

Extended nonnegative addition and multiplication satisfy the commutative semiring laws, including distributivity and zero absorption. Finite arithmetic is unchanged; a nonzero value times infinity is infinity, while 0·∞=0. Additive inverses and cancellation are not supplied: infinity+1 and infinity+2 both equal infinity. Compared with [Faris §2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Basic.lean#L143).

Reciprocal agrees with 1/r for positive finite values, sends zero to infinity, and sends infinity to zero. Lean defines it as the infimum of all b satisfying 1≤a·b. Thus reciprocal of zero here differs from reciprocal of zero in the ordinary nonnegative reals, which is zero. Compared with [Faris §2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Basic.lean#L177).

Division means multiplication by the extended reciprocal. A nonzero numerator divided by zero is infinity, but 0/0=0; every value divided by infinity is zero, including infinity/infinity. These total conventions extend ordinary positive-denominator division. They do not make [0,∞] a field or permit unrestricted cancellation. Compared with [Faris §2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Basic.lean#L179).

Subtraction is truncated: for finite a,b it is max(a−b,0). More generally it gives the least d with a≤d+b. Consequently infinity minus a finite value is infinity, while every value minus infinity is zero, including infinity−infinity. This is an ordered subtraction convention, not ordinary signed extended-real subtraction. Compared with [Faris §2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Basic.lean#L169).

The conversion from real to nonnegative real is the positive part max(r,0). It leaves nonnegative inputs unchanged and sends every negative input to zero. For example, −2 converts to 0, not 2: this operation is not absolute value and is not an embedding of all real numbers. Compared with [Faris §8.1](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/NNReal/Defs.lean#L157).

Subtraction of nonnegative reals is ordinary real subtraction followed by truncation at zero. Thus 2−5 is 0 in this type, while it is −3 in the real numbers. Converting a difference back to a real equals the ordinary difference only when the subtrahend does not exceed the minuend. Compared with [Faris §8.1](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/NNReal/Defs.lean#L81).

Nonnegative-real division is ordinary real division restricted to nonnegative inputs. Positive denominators give the familiar quotient; zero denominators give zero under Lean’s total real-division convention. Thus 5/0=0 here, unlike extended nonnegative reals, where 5/0=∞. No rounding or integer quotient is involved. Compared with [Faris §2.5](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/NNReal/Defs.lean#L102).

Strictly positive real numbers form a commutative multiplicative group, with zero adjoined as an absorbing element and the usual linear order. Every positive value has its ordinary reciprocal; zero’s reciprocal is defined as zero. Multiplication by a positive value preserves and reflects order. No additive inverses are asserted. Compared with [Faris §2.5](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/NNReal/Defs.lean#L126).

Extended nonnegative reals have associative, commutative addition with zero, together with the finite value one and natural-number values obtained by repeated addition. Every such natural-number value remains finite. Infinity is still absorbing under addition, so this structure does not assert subtraction or additive cancellation. Compared with [Faris §2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Basic.lean#L128).
